objects.description: Holds a choice string and its associated match score. Used to store search results for ranking and retrieval. Score semantics follow score_t from match.h. Ownership of str is unspecified in this header.

Container that manages a collection of choice strings, their scored search results, and iteration/selection state. Provides functions to initialize, populate from a FILE, add choices, run searches, navigate results, and destroy resources. Internal arrays include strings and scored results; buffer holds raw input. Concurrency may be controlled via worker_count.

Configuration for the choices/matching system, including UI and behavior toggles (e.g., showing scores/info), initial search text, prompt, worker count, input delimiter, and display parameters. Used to initialize choices via choices_init. String lifetimes are not specified here.
Floating-point score type used to represent match quality. Constants SCORE_MAX and SCORE_MIN correspond to +/-INFINITY. Used throughout matching and result scoring.

functions.name: choices_init
functions.description: Initializes a choices_t instance using the provided options. Sets up internal buffers, arrays, and state so other choices_* APIs can be used. Typical usage: declare a choices_t, call choices_init(&c, &opts), then add/read choices, search, and finally destroy.
requirements: c must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable memory for a choices_t structure.
options must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized options_t (use options_init/options_parse beforehand).
Must be called before any other choices_* function on c.
Do not call twice on the same c without an intervening choices_destroy.

functions.name: choices_fread
functions.description: Reads choices from a FILE stream into the choices_t container, splitting entries by input_delimiter. Intended to bulk-load choices (e.g., from stdin or a file) after initialization.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized choices_t (choices_init must have been called).
file must be a valid, open FILE* for reading and remain valid for the duration of the call.
input_delimiter is the character used to separate entries; behavior for special values is unspecified.
The function may allocate/expand internal storage; callers should not modify c internals directly.

functions.name: choices_destroy
functions.description: Releases resources owned by a choices_t instance and resets its state. Call after you are done using the choices container to avoid memory leaks.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized choices_t previously passed to choices_init.
After this call, c must not be used with other choices_* functions unless re-initialized with choices_init.
Safe to call exactly once per successful initialization; behavior on multiple destroys is unspecified.

functions.name: choices_add
functions.description: Adds a single choice string to the choices_t container for later searching and selection.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized choices_t (choices_init must have been called).
choice must be a valid, non-NULL, null-terminated string.
The string content is expected to remain valid if the implementation stores pointers directly; if it copies, this may not be required. Exact ownership semantics are unspecified.

functions.name: choices_available
functions.description: Returns the number of choices currently available for selection (e.g., after filtering/search).
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized choices_t.

functions.name: choices_search
functions.description: Performs a search/filter over the stored choices using the provided search string, likely updating the set/order of available results and their scores.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized choices_t containing zero or more added/loaded choices.
search must be a valid, non-NULL, null-terminated string.
Callers should expect subsequent calls to choices_get/choices_getscore/choices_available to reflect the updated search results.

functions.name: choices_get
functions.description: Retrieves the n-th available choice string from the current (possibly searched/filtered) results.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized choices_t.
n must be less than choices_available(c); otherwise behavior is undefined/unspecified.
Returned pointer refers to internal storage; do not free or modify it.

functions.name: choices_getscore
functions.description: Retrieves the score associated with the n-th available choice from the current search results. Higher or lower values may indicate better matches depending on the scoring scheme.
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized choices_t with a completed search state.
n must be less than choices_available(c); otherwise behavior is undefined/unspecified.
Callers must be prepared to handle special floating values as scores (e.g., SCORE_MAX/SCORE_MIN, which map to +/-INFINITY).

functions.name: choices_prev
functions.description: Moves the current selection to the previous available result (e.g., for UI navigation).
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized choices_t.
There should be at least one available choice; behavior when no choices are available is unspecified.
Selection index updates are within the available results’ bounds; exact wrap-around behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: choices_next
functions.description: Moves the current selection to the next available result (e.g., for UI navigation).
requirements: c must be a valid, initialized choices_t.
There should be at least one available choice; behavior when no choices are available is unspecified.
Selection index updates are within the available results’ bounds; exact wrap-around behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: options_init
functions.description: Initializes an options_t structure to default values. Typically called before options_parse or passing options to other components.
requirements: options must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable memory for an options_t.
Must be called before using options with other APIs that expect initialized options.

functions.name: options_parse
functions.description: Parses command-line style arguments and populates the options_t structure with the resulting configuration (e.g., flags like benchmark, workers, input_delimiter, etc.).
requirements: options must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an already initialized options_t (call options_init first).
argc must be non-negative and reflect the number of entries in argv.
argv must be a valid array of at least argc pointers to null-terminated strings. argv[argc] being NULL is typical but not required by this API specification.
The function may modify fields in options consistent with recognized arguments; unrecognized arguments handling is unspecified.

functions.name: has_match
functions.description: Returns a non-zero value if needle matches haystack according to the library’s matching criteria (likely fuzzy or subsequence matching), otherwise returns 0.
requirements: needle must be a valid, non-NULL, null-terminated string.
haystack must be a valid, non-NULL, null-terminated string.
Callers should not assume exact-match semantics; the precise matching algorithm is not documented here.

functions.name: match_positions
functions.signature: score_t match_positions(const char *needle, const char *haystack, size_t *positions);
functions.description: Computes a match score between needle and haystack and writes the matched character positions into positions. Returns the score as a score_t. Details of the scoring algorithm are not documented; SCORE_MAX/SCORE_MIN indicate extremes.
requirements: needle must be a valid, non-NULL, null-terminated string.
haystack must be a valid, non-NULL, null-terminated string.

positions must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable size_t storage for match indices; required capacity is not specified in the header. The presence of MATCH_MAX_LEN (1024) suggests an upper bound on positions that may be written.
Callers must be prepared to handle special score values including +/-INFINITY (SCORE_MAX/SCORE_MIN).

functions.name: match
functions.description: Computes and returns a match score between needle and haystack without returning positions. Suitable when only the score is needed.
requirements: needle must be a valid, non-NULL, null-terminated string.
haystack must be a valid, non-NULL, null-terminated string.
Callers must be prepared to handle special score values including +/-INFINITY (SCORE_MAX/SCORE_MIN).

endpoints.name: has_match
match_positions
match

data_types.description: A C-style string terminated by a NUL byte (\0). May contain arbitrary bytes except the terminator; typical text encodings like ASCII/UTF-8 are acceptable but not required. Must be memory-safe to read until the first NUL character.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a single bytes buffer intended to be split by the fuzzer
# into parameters for FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls. We design a compact container format
# that stores multiple null-terminated strings back-to-back. The fuzzer typically
# pulls out two strings (needle, haystack) per test case. We therefore emit a
# sequence of interesting needle/haystack pairs, each encoded as:
#   <needle bytes> 0x00 <haystack bytes> 0x00
# Repeated several times to allow the fuzzer to slice in different places.
# All strings are valid C strings (contain a terminating NUL) and try to cover
# different semantic cases for subsequence/fuzzy matching algorithms.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
PUNCT = "-_./:+@#%&*()[]{}<>?=,;!$^|~`\'\""
WS = " \t\r\n\v\f"


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(r.choice(ASCII) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_utf8(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII with some multi-byte UTF-8 codepoints
    # Choose from ranges: Latin-1 supplement, Greek, Cyrillic, Emoji subset
    pools = [
        (0x00A1, 0x00FF),  # Latin-1 supplement
        (0x0370, 0x03FF),  # Greek
        (0x0400, 0x04FF),  # Cyrillic
        (0x1F300, 0x1F64F),  # Misc Symbols and Pictographs + Emoticons
    ]
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            s.append(r.choice(ASCII))
        else:
            lo, hi = r.choice(pools)
            cp = r.randint(lo, hi)
            try:
                s.append(chr(cp))
            except ValueError:
                s.append("?")
    return "".join(s)


def _case_mix(s: str, r: random.Random) -> str:
    out = []
    for ch in s:
        if ch.isalpha() and r.random() < 0.5:
            out.append(ch.swapcase())
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return "".join(out)


def _repeat_with_gaps(token: str, r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create haystack with token characters spaced out among noise
    gap_chars = ASCII + PUNCT + WS
    out = []
    for ch in token:
        out.append(ch)
        # insert 0..3 random noise chars between
        for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)):
            out.append(r.choice(gap_chars))
    # Add some prefix/suffix noise
    prefix = "".join(r.choice(gap_chars) for _ in range(r.randint(0, 8)))
    suffix = "".join(r.choice(gap_chars) for _ in range(r.randint(0, 8)))
    return prefix + "".join(out) + suffix


def _path_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        name = _rand_ascii(r, 1, 8)
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            name += "." + r.choice(["c", "h", "cpp", "txt", "md", "json", "yaml"])  # extension
        parts.append(name)
    sep = "/"
    root = "/" if r.random() < 0.5 else ""
    return root + sep.join(parts)


def _email_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    user = _rand_ascii(r, 3, 10)
    dom = _rand_ascii(r, 3, 8).lower()
    tld = r.choice(["com", "org", "net", "io", "dev"]) if r.random() < 0.8 else _rand_ascii(r, 2, 3).lower()
    return f"{user}@{dom}.{tld}"


def _number_series(r: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    base = str(r.randint(0, 999999))
    return (base * ((length + len(base) - 1) // len(base)))[:length]


def _build_pairs(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    pairs: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Empty/degenerate cases
    pairs.append((b"\x00" + b"\x00"))  # needle="", haystack=""
    pairs.append((b"\x00" + b"nonempty\x00"))  # empty needle vs non-empty haystack
    pairs.append((b"nonempty\x00" + b"\x00"))  # non-empty needle vs empty haystack

    # 2) Exact match
    s = _rand_ascii(r, 1, 16)
    pairs.append((s.encode() + b"\x00" + s.encode() + b"\x00"))

    # 3) Case variation
    s2 = _rand_ascii(r, 3, 16)
    pairs.append((s2.encode() + b"\x00" + _case_mix(s2, r).encode() + b"\x00"))

    # 4) Subsequence with gaps and punctuation/whitespace
    tok = _rand_ascii(r, 2, 12)
    hay = _repeat_with_gaps(tok, r)
    pairs.append((tok.encode() + b"\x00" + hay.encode() + b"\x00"))

    # 5) Non-match variant (needle chars in reverse order)
    tok_rev = tok[::-1]
    pairs.append((tok_rev.encode() + b"\x00" + hay.encode() + b"\x00"))

    # 6) Unicode/UTF-8 content
    n_utf = _rand_utf8(r, 2, 12)
    h_utf = _repeat_with_gaps(n_utf, r)
    pairs.append((n_utf.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00" + h_utf.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"))

    # 7) Haystack with long length, needle short
    needle_short = _rand_ascii(r, 1, 4)
    long_hay = _rand_ascii(r, 100, 300) + r.choice(["", PUNCT, WS])
    pairs.append((needle_short.encode() + b"\x00" + long_hay.encode() + b"\x00"))

    # 8) Path-like strings
    needle_path_tok = r.choice(["src", "include", "bin", "lib", "test"])[: r.randint(2, 4)]
    hay_path = _path_like(r)
    pairs.append((needle_path_tok.encode() + b"\x00" + hay_path.encode() + b"\x00"))

    # 9) Email-like
    nn = r.choice(["@", ".", "+", "-"])
    pairs.append((nn.encode() + b"\x00" + _email_like(r).encode() + b"\x00"))

    # 10) Repeated characters and numbers
    ch = r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase)
    needle_rep = ch * r.randint(1, 8)
    hay_rep = (ch * r.randint(5, 40))
    pairs.append((needle_rep.encode() + b"\x00" + hay_rep.encode() + b"\x00"))

    # 11) Numeric series
    num_len = r.randint(5, 20)
    nn2 = _number_series(r, r.randint(1, 6))
    hh2 = _number_series(r, num_len)
    pairs.append((nn2.encode() + b"\x00" + hh2.encode() + b"\x00"))

    # 12) Mixed whitespace tokens
    n_ws = r.choice([" ", "\t", "\n", " \t", "\r\n"]) * r.randint(1, 3)
    h_ws = _repeat_with_gaps(n_ws, r)
    pairs.append((n_ws.encode() + b"\x00" + h_ws.encode() + b"\x00"))

    # 13) Needles longer than haystack
    n_long = _rand_ascii(r, 20, 40)
    h_short = _rand_ascii(r, 1, 5)
    pairs.append((n_long.encode() + b"\x00" + h_short.encode() + b"\x00"))

    # 14) Special punctuation-heavy
    n_p = "".join(r.choice(PUNCT) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 8)))
    h_p = _repeat_with_gaps(n_p, r)
    pairs.append((n_p.encode() + b"\x00" + h_p.encode() + b"\x00"))

    # 15) Overlapping tokens inside haystack
    token = "aba" if r.random() < 0.5 else "101"
    hay_ov = (token * r.randint(2, 8))
    pairs.append((token.encode() + b"\x00" + hay_ov.encode() + b"\x00"))

    return pairs


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a sequence of needle/haystack pairs; concatenate to one buffer.
    parts = _build_pairs(r)

    # Optionally add some random additional pairs to increase diversity, while
    # keeping total under MAX_TOTAL.
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 5)):
        # random freestyle pair
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            n = _rand_ascii(r, 0, 20)
            h = _rand_ascii(r, 0, 200)
        else:
            n = _rand_utf8(r, 0, 16)
            h = _rand_utf8(r, 0, 200)
        parts.append(n.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00" + h.encode("utf-8") + b"\x00")

    buf = b"".join(parts)

    # Ensure we do not exceed MAX_TOTAL; if too large, truncate at a safe boundary.
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL:
        # Try to trim to the last completed NUL-terminated string boundary within limit
        trimmed = buf[:MAX_TOTAL]
        # Ensure the buffer ends with a NUL terminator to not cut a string unterminated
        if not trimmed.endswith(b"\x00"):
            # Find last NUL within trimmed
            idx = trimmed.rfind(b"\x00")
            if idx != -1:
                trimmed = trimmed[: idx + 1]
            else:
                # If somehow no NUL (unlikely), force terminator
                trimmed = trimmed[:-1] + b"\x00"
        buf = trimmed

    return buf
